tagline.text: One of southern Manila's biggest family-friendly malls, in the heart of Filinvest City

location.label: Location
location.text: Corporate Avenue, Filinvest City, Alabang, Muntinlupa, Metro Manila

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (a great indoor option on rainy days; December–February is the most comfortable)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day to a full day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–3,000 (food and play areas, excluding shopping, per person)

children.text: This large mall in Filinvest City opened in 1998 and was formerly known as Festival Supermall. It consists of the West Wing, the East Wing and the riverside River Park, and puts department stores, restaurants, indoor play centers and Gold Class cinemas in one place.

Festival Mall Alabang is a large shopping mall in Filinvest City (formerly Filinvest Corporate City) in Alabang, Muntinlupa, in the south of Metro Manila. According to English Wikipedia, it is owned and operated by Filinvest Land and opened on May 15, 1998. It was formerly called Festival Supermall, and many locals still use that name or simply call it "Festi." It is a different place from Alabang Town Center, the mall in the Ayala Alabang area of the same district, so double-check the address before you set off.

The mall has three main parts: the West Wing (the main mall, built in 1998), the East Wing added in 2017, and River Park, an outdoor area that stretches along the river apart from the main building. Wikipedia gives a gross floor area of roughly 400,000 square meters, with four upper floors and one basement level, which places it among the largest malls in the Philippines. The number of stores varies by source, from about 800 to more than 1,000, so rather than rely on an exact figure, just know that it is too big to see in a single day.

For travelers, the appeal is that everything is in one place. You will find Robinsons and Landmark department stores, supermarkets such as Savemore and Shopwise, fashion stores like H&M, Nike and Levi's, a dining scene that runs from Starbucks, Jollibee and McDonald's to ramen, udon and American-style family restaurants, children's play centers, and everyday services such as banks and parcel couriers. It feels relatively laid-back compared with the malls in northern Manila, and the many local families make it easy to get around with kids.

It is more a place for shopping and relaxing than a sightseeing spot, but it does have a few things to look at: an Art Deco former Department of Health building from 1924 that was restored in 2009 and folded into the mall, and a Marian chapel on a riverside hill that opened to the public in October 2022. Opening hours, tenants and the cinema situation change often, so check the official channels before you go.

blocks.title: West Wing, East Wing and River Park

children.text: The West Wing is the main mall that opened in 1998, and the East Wing is the extension added in 2017. The East Wing has a Water Garden, and its Landmark supermarket opened in July 2017 and the Landmark department store in October of the same year. The floors are labeled Lower Ground (roughly a basement level), Upper Ground, 2nd and 3rd. It is easy to get lost, so snap a photo of the directory map when you first arrive.

The West Wing has X-Site, an indoor amusement center for teens, and Pixie Forest, an indoor amusement center for younger children. X-Site has rides such as a roller coaster and bumper cars plus arcade games, while Pixie Forest focuses on toddler rides such as a carousel and a train. Other play spaces listed include Kidzooona, Timezone and a trampoline park. On a rainy day with kids, this is the most dependable option in Alabang.

Two Gold Class cinemas, each with 186 seats, opened on the 3rd floor of the East Wing on July 25, 2018. They are the standout premium screens in the East Wing. On the other hand, the regular cinemas in the West Wing have reportedly been partly inactive since 2024, and the number of screens differs by source, so if you plan to watch a film, check that day's showtimes on the official channels.

This outdoor riverside area was completed in 2014 as part of a renovation project that began in 2013. A wooden boardwalk, bike paths, restaurants and shops run along it, and it is best for a stroll in the late afternoon as the sun begins to drop rather than in the heat of the day. It is also spacious enough for children to run around.

This Catholic chapel sits in the hillside gardens of River Park and opened to the public in October 2022. It was designed by Japanese architect Hiroshi Nakamura with NAP Architects, and is said to have a spire about 30 meters tall and seating for 300. Mass is held on Saturdays and Sundays, and it is reportedly open to everyone during mall hours. Its white, lily-like shape makes it a popular photo spot.

This Art Deco building, built in 1924 and once used as the Department of Health's biological production service building, was restored in 2009 and now serves as part of the mall. Right beside it stands a replica of José Rizal's clay sculpture "The Triumph of Science over Death." It is a quick way to catch a bit of history within your shopping route.

The food court is large, and the official Filinvest Malls directory lists chains such as Starbucks, Jollibee, McDonald's, Chili's, California Pizza Kitchen, Ramen Nagi and Marugame Udon. Specialty restaurants such as a Brazilian barbecue buffet are also listed. It is especially handy when a family cannot agree on a single menu.

There are bank branches and ATMs, a parcel courier outlet, and a regional Department of Foreign Affairs office that handles passports (reportedly moved into the East Wing in 2025), which is useful for long-term residents too. Savemore, Shopwise and the Landmark supermarket are good for snacks and daily necessities, and there are brand stores such as Samsung and Sony for electronics. Office locations for government services can change, so check before you visit.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: From lunch to a riverside walk

children.text: Enter through the West Wing main entrance or the connecting walkway from the South Station side, and check the directory map. Start with an early lunch at the Lower Ground food court or the dining area.
Shop your way around the Upper Ground and 2nd floors. If you have children, fit in a play area such as Pixie Forest or Kidzooona at this time.
Move over to the East Wing Water Garden and rest with a coffee. It is also worth checking the Gold Class showtimes on the 3rd floor of the East Wing.
Head outside to River Park, walk the boardwalk and climb up to Our Lady of Lourdes Chapel on the hill.
Finish with dinner at a River Park restaurant. The mall normally closes at 9:00 PM, so decide on your return time in advance.
The mall is big, so seeing both the West and East Wings takes a fair amount of walking. Comfortable shoes are a must.

items.title: Full-day route
items.subtitle: A tour of southern Manila shopping

children.text: Arrive shortly after opening, when it is quiet, and see the Art Deco building and the Rizal statue first.
Take your time exploring the West Wing shops and play centers.
Have lunch at the food court or an East Wing restaurant.
Take a Grab or taxi to nearby Alabang Town Center or Molito Lifestyle Center for coffee and snacks.
Return to Filinvest City for an evening walk and dinner at River Park, then head back to your hotel.
The mall and hotels inside Filinvest City are close to one another, but traffic builds up at rush hour, so allow plenty of travel time.
A local blog says buses run from Makati and EDSA toward Metropolis Mall and Alabang, and that routes from Lawton run via Taft Avenue and PGH to Alabang.
Wikipedia lists bus routes 10 and 24, South Station and a Premium P2P service as transport near the mall. Timetables and fares change often, so check the operator's notices.
If you take a bus or UV Express, get off at Alabang South Station and walk the connecting walkway into the mall. Travel time varies a lot with the starting point and traffic, so allow plenty of time.
Wikipedia records the Alabang PNR station as closed since March 2024, so it is safer not to rely on the train.
From Manila, Makati or BGC, a Grab or taxi is the easiest option; set the destination to the Festival Mall main entrance. Fares vary a great deal with the time of day and traffic, so check the app.

If you drive, use the Alabang exit of the SLEX and search for Festival Mall in your navigation app. Parking is described as plentiful inside and around the mall, and Wikipedia gives more than 4,000 slots.
From NAIA airport, some guides say it takes about 25 minutes toward the SLEX, but traffic can easily double that.
Jeepney routes pass in front of the mall, and Alabang South Station connects to it by a walkway.
Some hotels and offices inside Filinvest City are within walking distance.
Alabang Town Center and Molito are away from the mall, so Grab is the simplest choice.

Because it is mostly indoors, you can visit at any time of year, and it works especially well as an alternative on rainy or very hot days. Walks in the outdoor River Park, however, depend on the weather.
It gets very crowded, and parking takes a long time, during the Christmas season, year-end sales and weekend afternoons. For a quieter visit, go on a weekday daytime or shortly after opening.

There are several hotels in and around Filinvest City, and the wider Alabang area has a range of hotels. Access to the SLEX and the Skyway is good for getting to the airport or central Manila. Hotel rates vary greatly by date, so check booking sites directly.

Meals can all be handled inside the mall, and if you miss Korean food there are Korean restaurants around Alabang; check a map app for current opening status. Outside the mall, Molito Lifestyle Center is known for cafes and restaurants such as Wildflour and Manam, and some places stay open until 11:00 PM or midnight.
The mall has several entrances, so decide in your map app whether your destination is the Festival Mall main entrance or the South Station connecting walkway, to avoid confusion.
Hours are generally 10:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily, though some listings show longer weekend hours. Confirm through the official channels.
The mall is very large, so take a photo of the store directory map at first to make finding your way easier.
Pixie Forest and Kidzooona are good when it rains and you have no other plan for the kids.
For movies, the Gold Class screens on the 3rd floor of the East Wing are the safest bet; the regular West Wing screens may be closed, so check before booking.
For a River Park walk, avoid the hot daytime and go in the late afternoon for a more comfortable time.
Passport or consular services can change location, so confirm through official notices before visiting.
Cinema operations, tenant lineup and opening hours change often and differ by source. Check the mall's official channels for the latest notices before you go.
Watch out for pickpockets and phone snatchers, and carry your bag in front of you.
In the Christmas season and on weekends, just getting into the parking lot can take a long time.
The Alabang PNR station is reported to be closed since March 2024, so do not plan on train travel.
During typhoons or heavy rain, roads around Alabang can be blocked or flooded, so check the weather forecast.
The number of cinema screens and the prices of play areas differ by source and need to be confirmed locally.

A shopping complex in the Alabang area that opened in 1982 and is reached by Grab. It is known for its open-air layout and restaurant row, but some zones may be under redevelopment, so check before you go.
An open-air dining and cafe strip on Madrigal Avenue, with some places open until late. It is roughly a 10-minute drive from Filinvest City (depending on traffic), so take a Grab.
